{{Short description|Attractor in dynamical systems theory}}
[[File:Thomas' cyclically symmetric attractor.png|thumb|Thomas' cyclically symmetric attractor.]]In the [[dynamical systems theory]], '''Thomas' cyclically symmetric attractor''' is a 3D [[strange attractor]] originally proposed by [[René Thomas (biologist)|René Thomas]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Thomas |first=René |year=1999 |title=Deterministic chaos seen in terms of feedback circuits: Analysis, synthesis, 'labyrinth chaos' |journal=Int. J. Bifurc. Chaos |volume=9 |issue=10 |pages=1889–1905 |doi=10.1142/S0218127499001383|bibcode=1999IJBC....9.1889T }}</ref> It has a simple form which is cyclically symmetric in the x, y, and z variables and can be viewed as the trajectory of a frictionally dampened particle moving in a 3D lattice of forces.<ref name="sprott">{{cite journal |first1=J. C. |last1=Sprott |first2=Konstantinos E. |last2=Chlouverakis |title=Labyrinth Chaos |journal=Int. J. Bifurc. Chaos |volume=17 |issue=6 |pages=2097 |year=2007 |doi=10.1142/S0218127407018245|bibcode=2007IJBC...17.2097S }}</ref> The simple form has made it a popular example.

It is described by the differential equations
:<math>\frac{dx}{dt} = \sin(y)-bx</math>
:<math>\frac{dy}{dt} = \sin(z)-by</math>
:<math>\frac{dz}{dt} = \sin(x)-bz</math>
where <math>b</math> is a constant.

<math>b</math> corresponds to how [[dissipative]] the system is, and acts as a [[Bifurcation theory|bifurcation]] parameter. For <math>b>1</math> the origin is the single stable equilibrium. At <math>b=1</math> it undergoes a [[pitchfork bifurcation]], splitting into two attractive fixed points. As the parameter is decreased further they undergo a [[Hopf bifurcation]] at <math>b\approx 0.32899</math>, creating a stable limit cycle. The limit cycle then undergoes a [[Period-doubling bifurcation|period doubling cascade]] and becomes chaotic at <math>b\approx 0.208186</math>. Beyond this the attractor expands, undergoing a series of [[Crisis (dynamical systems)|crises]] (up to six separate attractors can coexist for certain values). The [[fractal dimension]] of the attractor increases towards 3.<ref name="sprott"/>

In the limit <math>b=0</math> the system lacks dissipation and the trajectory [[Ergodic theory|ergodically]] wanders the entire space (with an exception for 1.67%, where it drifts parallel to one of the coordinate axes: this corresponds to [[quasiperiodic]] torii). The dynamics has been described as deterministic fractional [[Brownian motion]], and exhibits [[anomalous diffusion]].<ref name="sprott"/><ref>{{cite journal |first1=G. |last1=Rowlands |first2=J. C. |last2=Sprott |title=A simple diffusion model showing anomalous scaling |journal=Physics of Plasmas |volume=15 |pages=082308 |year=2008 |issue=8 |doi=10.1063/1.2969429|bibcode=2008PhPl...15h2308R }}</ref>
